About WalmartWalmart Inc. (Nasdaq: WMT) is a people-led, tech-powered omnichannel retailer helping people save money and live better - anytime and anywhere - in stores, online, and through their mobile devices. Each week, approximately 280 million customers and members visit more than 10,900 stores and numerous eCommerce websites in 19 countries. With fiscal year 2026 revenue of $713 billion, Walmart employs approximately 2.1 million associates worldwide. Walmart continues to be a leader in sustainability, corporate philanthropy, and employment opportunity. desk.headline: Revenue up 5.2% to $188.8bn and adjusted EPS $0.65, both beat; full-year outlook raised for the third time
results: Total revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8bn (4.5% in constant currency); the shift of Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale into Q4 held back growth.
Walmart U.S. sales grew 3.6% to $125.0bn with comp sales up 2.9%; lower drug prices under federal price caps cut about 70 bps from comps.
Online keeps driving growth: global eCommerce up 17%, U.S. eCommerce up 23%, U.S. advertising up 37% and membership fee income up 17%.
Gross margin rose 28 bps to 24.5%; operating income jumped 16% to $7.8bn, partly because last year carried a $0.7bn PhonePe pay charge.
GAAP EPS fell to $0.62 from $0.77 on investment losses; $2.7bn of shares were bought back in the quarter and inventory rose 8.1% to $70.6bn.

guidance.summary: Walmart lifted its full-year outlook again: sales growth of 4.9–5.2% and adjusted EPS of $2.84–2.89. The top of the EPS range only matches the FactSet consensus, and the implied sales range sits slightly below it.

points: CEO John Furner called shoppers "stable" and "resilient", with grocery share gains among the biggest in three years.
Q4 guided to sales growth of 4.5–5.5% (cc) and adjusted EPS of $0.73–0.78, helped about 100 bps by the Big Billion Days timing shift.
CFO John David Rainey said diesel and transport will add over $2bn of extra costs this year.
The new $120 Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus bundle, launched 20 October, brought in a couple of million new Sam's Club members.
U.S. eCommerce is now profitable at the margin, with incremental margins above 12%; price rollbacks fell to about 7,700 from over 11,000.
